A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyperAdapt by the same authors. All 17 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v3, including Appendix A, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original fine-tuning results, empirical rank measurements, and learning-rate experiments. Although some baseline results are explicitly borrowed, the work reports its own empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds GLUE evaluations, rank-1 baseline results, diagonal-factor ablations, and experiments with randomly initialized RoBERTa.

M1.justification: HyperAdapt remains W'=AW0B with two identity-initialized diagonal factors, n+m trainable parameters, and precomputable adapted weights. The method equations and Listing 1 are unchanged. The new one-factor variants are presented as ablations.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands GLUE coverage from six tasks to eight by adding QQP and MNLI, explicitly excluded in v2. Math10K, Commonsense170K, s1, and their evaluation tasks remain unchanged. The scratch experiment reuses GLUE with a different model initialization.

E2.justification: v3 adds LoRA r=1 to the GLUE comparison in Table 1 and DoRA r=1 to arithmetic reasoning and reasoning-trace evaluation in Tables 2 and 4. BoFT has no result row in either version, so removing its appendix settings does not establish removal of an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New Section 6.3 introduces random-initialization experiments targeting attention and MLP linear layers, with other layers frozen even for the restricted Full comparator. Section 6.2 adds A-only and B-only controls. Appendix Table 5 in v2 becomes Table 7 in v3 and changes stated HyperAdapt/VeRA learning rates for CoLA from 8e-3 to 6e-3 and RTE from 8e-3 to 3e-3. Whether existing experiments were rerun is unstated.

E4.justification: New Sections 6.2–6.3 substantially extend the analyses by testing the contribution of each diagonal factor and dependence on pretrained knowledge. Table 5 compares A-only, B-only, and joint adaptation; Table 6 reports scratch GLUE experiments, supplemented by an alternate-learning-rate check for Full. Earlier rank and learning-rate analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation statement in Section 5.1. Added GLUE results use the existing uncertainty format; no new statistical procedure or explicit increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for the expanded coverage, rank-1 comparisons, and Tables 5–6. Joint adaptation scores 75.5 versus 71.6 for A-only and 70.7 for B-only. Existing LoRA GLUE values are replaced, including CoLA 68.2±1.9 becoming 65.5±0.8. HyperAdapt's shared benchmark entries remain fixed; its GLUE average changes from 86.0 to 86.9 with the expanded task set. Figure 4 also corrects the attribution of the plotted spectra.

T1.justification: Section 4 newly states a comparative rank bound for one-sided IA3/scale-and-shift updates, rank(Delta W) ≤ rank(W), against HyperAdapt's bound of 2·rank(W). Lemma 1, its proof, and the normalized-rank definition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's competitive-performance contribution drops full fine-tuning from that bullet and emphasizes ultra-low parameter regimes. This modestly qualifies the contribution framing; the abstract and conclusion retain the central parameter-efficiency and high-rank adaptation claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations supporting joint diagonal scaling and relative competitiveness without pretraining despite poor absolute performance. Section 5.2 replaces the speculation about lower data contamination in Llama-3 with a cross-model robustness interpretation. The concluding limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds GLUE LoRA and LoRA r=1 hyperparameters, QQP/MNLI schedules, and DoRA r=1 settings for arithmetic and reasoning-trace experiments. It removes the BoFT hyperparameter block. Section 6.1 newly identifies Qwen-2.5-7B as the model used in the existing learning-rate sweep.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to IA3 (Liu et al., 2022) and Scaling & Shifting Your Features (Lian et al., 2023). Section 4 positions HyperAdapt's two-sided scaling against these one-sided approaches and connects that distinction to the new ablation.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. v3 adds Sections 6.2–6.3, makes localized wording edits, and changes the preprint header to a publication header. The arithmetic-reasoning appendix subheading disappears, but its explanatory paragraph and hyperparameter table remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds two result tables and expands existing result and hyperparameter tables with rows or columns. Figure 4 is reformatted and its swapped color labels are corrected: blue becomes HyperAdapt and green LoRA, matching the caption. Figure 5 moves beside the sensitivity discussion. The other figures' graphics and overall visual style are retained.

improvement.justification: The new component ablation and low-budget comparisons better support the design, while Figure 4's corrected legend resolves a contradiction with the rank analysis. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.1 still quotes the old 86.0 average despite Table 1's 86.9, and the revised GLUE learning rates and replaced LoRA scores remain unexplained.
